task_3.title: Preserve ANSI-colored failure reasons when pytrace is disabled
task_3.description: The 8.3.4 update fixes pytest's terminal rendering for value-only failures so ANSI-colored text in failure reasons is preserved when stack traces are suppressed. This makes `pytest.fail()` output consistent between `pytrace=True` and `pytrace=False` for colored terminal messages.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `pytest.fail()` preserves ANSI-colored failure reasons when called with `pytrace=False`, so users see correctly formatted terminal output instead of partially exposed escape-code fragments.

expectation.grounded: When `pytest.fail(reason=..., pytrace=False)` renders a failure reason through pytest's value-style terminal representation, ANSI escape sequences in the supplied reason should be emitted as-is so the terminal can interpret them correctly. Value-style output should preserve the original text content and line boundaries rather than stripping indentation or rewriting the content as source-highlighted lines.
expectation.conceptual: Failures reported without a traceback should display colored or otherwise ANSI-formatted reason text the same way as other pytest failure output. If the user includes terminal formatting in the failure reason, pytest should show the intended formatted text instead of leaking raw control-sequence fragments.

constraints.grounded: The fix should apply specifically to value-style failure rendering and must not change the existing terminal formatting behavior for non-value traceback/source representations. Multi-line value output should remain in order and preserve explicit newline separation between lines.
constraints.conceptual: Only the affected value-only failure presentation should change. Other traceback and source-display behavior should remain unchanged, and formatted failure text should still appear exactly in the order and line structure provided by the caller.

behavior: `pytest.fail()` with `pytrace=False` should preserve ANSI escape sequences embedded in the failure reason so terminal color or styling is rendered correctly.
Value-only failure output should be written directly as plain terminal text instead of being passed through source-style formatting logic that can expose raw escape-code fragments.
For multi-line failure reasons rendered without traceback details, pytest should preserve each line's content and emit line breaks consistently.
acceptance_criteria: When a test calls `pytest.fail()` with `pytrace=False` and a reason containing ANSI color sequences, the failure output should render the intended terminal styling instead of showing broken escape-code text.
When the same formatted reason is used with traceback-suppressed failure output, the visible formatting behavior should be consistent with pytest's normal colored failure rendering.
When a value-only failure reason contains multiple lines, pytest should display the lines in the original order with the expected line separation.
When pytest renders non-value traceback or source sections, their existing formatting behavior should remain unchanged by this fix.

task_2.title: Preserve source ranges in rewritten pytest assertions
task_2.description: Pytest 8.3.4 fixes assertion rewriting so rewritten assert expressions preserve the original source locations of user-written subexpressions. This restores compatibility with AST- and instruction-position-aware tooling that needs accurate source mapping inside assertions, while still allowing pytest to attach locations to generated helper nodes that do not already have them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest assertion rewriting preserves the original source ranges of user-written expressions inside rewritten `assert` statements so tools that inspect AST or instruction positions continue to identify the correct source locations within assertions.

expectation.grounded: When pytest rewrites `assert` statements, expression nodes that already correspond to user code should retain their original source location metadata rather than being reassigned to the full `assert` statement range. This applies to rewritten expressions involved in operations such as unary operators, binary operators, function calls, attribute access, comparisons, and temporary names returned from rewritten subexpressions. Generated nodes that have no existing location may still receive the enclosing assertion location.
expectation.conceptual: Assertion rewriting should remain transparent to source-location-aware tools. After rewriting, code inside an `assert` should still appear to come from the original expression spans that the user wrote, not from a single location covering the whole assertion.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress normal assertion rewriting behavior or remove location data from generated helper nodes. Only nodes lacking source location information may fall back to the enclosing `assert` location; nodes with valid original positions must keep them.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve source mapping accuracy inside rewritten assertions without changing the intended assertion evaluation behavior or broadly reassigning locations for unrelated generated nodes.

behavior: Rewritten `assert` expressions preserve existing line and column range metadata for user-originated subexpressions instead of overwriting them with the enclosing assertion span.
Temporary expression names produced during rewriting inherit the source location of the originating expression they represent.
Rewritten unary operations, binary operations, function calls, attribute lookups, and comparison expressions retain the source location of the original user-written expression.
Pytest only applies the enclosing assertion location to generated AST nodes that do not already have source location metadata.
Tools that depend on AST or instruction position metadata can observe the same source mapping inside rewritten assertions as in the original unrewritten code.
acceptance_criteria: When a rewritten `assert` contains user-written subexpressions, those subexpressions should report their original source ranges rather than the range of the full `assert` statement.

When pytest rewrites assertions containing operators, calls, attribute access, or comparisons, source-location-aware tooling should still resolve those operations to their original positions inside the assertion.
When rewriting introduces helper nodes with no prior source position, pytest should still provide usable location information for those generated nodes.
When assertion rewriting runs on code that relies on AST or instruction position mapping, behavior inside `assert` statements should remain compatible with the original source layout.

task_1.title: Fix importlib collection for nested same-name directories
task_1.description: Pytest 8.3.4 fixes an importlib-mode collection failure that could crash with an internal KeyError when a test directory contains a child directory with the same name. The update makes parent-module and namespace-package resolution behave correctly so affected test modules can be collected normally.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running pytest with `--import-mode=importlib` can collect test modules in nested directory layouts where a directory contains a child directory with the same name, without crashing during import resolution.

expectation.grounded: Under `--import-mode=importlib`, pytest should resolve and import any missing parent modules before importing the target test module, and it should recognize both regular packages and namespace packages as valid parents. Collection should succeed for nested same-name directory layouts instead of surfacing an internal `KeyError` from importlib.
expectation.conceptual: Importlib-based collection should work reliably for nested test locations, including unusual but valid directory structures. Users should get normal collection behavior rather than an internal crash when parent directories need to be interpreted as packages or namespace packages.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve existing `--import-mode=importlib` behavior for both package parents (directories with `__init__.py`) and namespace-package parents (directories without `__init__.py`). Import resolution must continue to accept both file-backed modules and directory-backed namespace packages, and importing the target module must remain compatible with the standard parent-child module hierarchy exposed through Python imports.
constraints.conceptual: The change should remove the erroneous crash without regressing normal importlib-mode collection. Standard package imports and namespace-style imports should both continue to work in the same collection flow.

behavior: When importing a test module in `--import-mode=importlib`, pytest now imports unresolved parent modules before importing the target module.
Parent modules are resolved correctly whether the target is a normal module file, a package module, or a module located under namespace-package directories.
Namespace packages are treated as valid import targets during spec matching even when their module spec has no file origin and is represented by search locations for a directory.
Directory-backed namespace parents can be loaded with a usable module spec, allowing collection to proceed in layouts that previously failed.
As a result, nested layouts where a directory contains a child directory with the same name no longer fail with an internal `KeyError` during collection.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is run with `--import-mode=importlib` against a test module inside a directory that also contains a child directory with the same name, collection should complete without an internal `KeyError`.
When parent directories in that import path contain `__init__.py`, pytest should continue to treat them as regular packages and import the target module successfully.
When parent directories in that import path do not contain `__init__.py`, pytest should still resolve them as namespace packages and import the target module successfully.

When a nested test module is imported in importlib mode, its imported parent modules should be available through the expected Python module hierarchy rather than failing during parent-path resolution.

task_5.title: Clarify pytest.Config.getoption fallback semantics
task_5.description: Version 8.3.4 clarifies the documented behavior of pytest's Config.getoption API. The update makes explicit that the default argument is only used when an option was never declared, while declared options still return their actual value even when that value is None; it also clarifies how skip interacts with default.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the documented upgrade behavior for `pytest.Config.getoption()` clearly distinguishes between undeclared options and declared options with a `None` value, so users do not expect the `default` argument to override a declared option's `None` result.

expectation.grounded: `pytest.Config.getoption(name, default=..., skip=...)` must be specified as using `default` only when the requested option was not declared through `pytest_addoption`. If the option was declared, `getoption()` should return the option's actual value, including `None`, instead of substituting `default`. When `skip=True`, an undeclared option or a declared option with value `None` is treated as skippable, except that an explicitly provided `default` is returned instead of skipping.
expectation.conceptual: The API contract should make clear that a fallback value applies only to missing option definitions, not to declared options whose current value happens to be empty. Skip behavior should also be documented so callers know that providing a fallback takes precedence over skipping.

constraints.grounded: Do not redefine `default` as a general replacement for `None` values. Preserve the distinction between an undeclared option and a declared option with no effective value. Preserve the documented precedence that an explicit `default` suppresses a skip result.
constraints.conceptual: The clarification must avoid changing established behavior expectations for existing callers. It should narrow ambiguity without implying a new runtime feature or a broader fallback policy.

behavior: `pytest.Config.getoption()` treats `default` as a fallback for undeclared options, not as an override for declared options.
If a declared option currently resolves to `None`, `getoption()` returns `None` when called without `skip=True`, even if `default` is provided.
If `skip=True` is used and the option is undeclared or resolves to `None`, an explicit `default` value is returned instead of triggering a skip.
The 8.3.4 update is a clarification of the public API contract and does not introduce a runtime implementation change in the diff provided.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller reads an undeclared option with `pytest.Config.getoption()` and provides `default`, the documented contract states that the fallback value is returned.
When a caller reads a declared option whose value is `None` and provides `default` without enabling skip, the documented contract states that the result remains `None`.
When a caller enables `skip=True` and also provides `default`, the documented contract states that the fallback value takes precedence over skipping.

When users consult the upgrade note for 8.3.4, they can distinguish between missing option declarations and declared options with `None` values without inferring a behavior change beyond documentation clarification.

task_4.title: Treat boolean values as exact matches in pytest.approx
task_4.description: The 8.3.4 update changes pytest.approx() so boolean values are no longer treated as numeric inputs for tolerant comparisons. Boolean expectations now use strict equality across scalar and container comparisons, and failed comparisons continue to report mismatch information without crashing when relative-difference calculation is not valid.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest.approx() compares boolean values using exact equality instead of numeric tolerance semantics, so boolean fields in scalar, sequence, and mapping comparisons only match the same boolean value and failed comparisons remain reportable.

expectation.grounded: When pytest.approx() is given a boolean expected value, ApproxScalar should treat that value as non-numeric and only consider it equal to the same boolean value. Numeric values such as 1 or 0 must not match boolean expectations through tolerant comparison. This strict-boolean behavior must also apply when booleans appear inside mappings or other supported composite values handled by pytest.approx(). On comparison failure, pytest.approx() should still produce comparison output instead of failing while computing relative-difference metadata for zero-like expected values.
expectation.conceptual: Boolean values passed through pytest.approx() should behave like exact logical flags, not like numbers with tolerance. A comparison should only succeed when the boolean value actually matches, including inside larger structures, and a mismatch should be reported as a normal comparison failure.

constraints.grounded: Do not change tolerant comparison behavior for supported numeric types such as complex numbers and Decimal values beyond excluding bool from numeric tolerance handling. Non-boolean non-numeric values should continue to use strict equality fallback semantics. Failure reporting for mismatches must remain available even when relative-difference calculation cannot be performed.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing approximate comparison behavior for real numeric data, while carving out booleans as exact-only values. Preserve ordinary strict-equality behavior for non-numeric content and ensure mismatches are reported robustly rather than turning into separate runtime errors.

behavior: A boolean expected value in pytest.approx() is compared by strict equality rather than numeric tolerance.
A non-boolean numeric actual value does not satisfy a boolean expectation in pytest.approx(), even if it is numerically equivalent to True or False.
Booleans nested inside mappings or other supported composite comparisons follow the same exact-match rule.
Stringification and mismatch reporting for boolean expectations no longer present them as tolerance-based numeric approximations.

When a composite approx comparison fails and relative-difference computation is not valid for an expected zero-like value, pytest.approx() still reports the mismatch instead of raising an internal error.
acceptance_criteria: When comparing a scalar boolean with pytest.approx(), it should succeed only if the actual value is the same boolean.
When comparing a scalar boolean expectation with a numeric value such as 1 or 0, pytest.approx() should report inequality.
When comparing mappings or sequences containing boolean members with pytest.approx(), differing boolean members should cause the overall comparison to fail even if a tolerance is provided.
When a boolean comparison through pytest.approx() fails, the failure should be surfaced as a comparison mismatch rather than as a tolerance-based boolean approximation.
When a composite approx comparison includes an expected zero-like value and the comparison fails, mismatch reporting should still complete without raising an additional arithmetic error.

task_6.title: Clarify tmp_path and --basetemp retention behavior
task_6.description: The 8.3.4 update improves the user-facing documentation for pytest temporary directories. It centralizes the description of base temporary directory handling and retention, and clarifies that using `--basetemp` does not provide retained directories across runs under the current behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest's temporary-directory documentation clearly explains how `tmp_path` and `tmpdir` are created under a base temporary directory, how retention is configured in general, and that `--basetemp` continues to use non-retained per-run cleanup behavior.

expectation.grounded: The public documentation for `TempPathFactory`, `tmp_path`, and `tmpdir` should describe these temporary directories in terms of the shared temporary-directory location and retention model. `tmp_path` should be documented as returning a unique `pathlib.Path` per test invocation, `tmpdir` should be documented as returning the legacy path equivalent, and both should refer users to the central retention guidance instead of duplicating partial rules inline. The documented behavior must remain consistent with the current handling of `--basetemp`, where retention across runs is not provided.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to understand, from the official temporary-directory documentation and fixture descriptions, where per-test temporary directories live, that retention is configurable in the normal model, and that selecting a custom base temp directory with `--basetemp` still does not keep prior runs.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce or imply a runtime change to temporary-directory creation or retention. Preserve the existing `tmp_path` and `tmpdir` fixture contracts, including unique per-invocation directories under a base temp directory, and preserve the current no-retention-across-runs semantics for `--basetemp`.
constraints.conceptual: This update must clarify behavior without changing how temporary directories actually work. Existing temporary-directory lifecycle and cleanup behavior should stay the same.

behavior: The `TempPathFactory` documentation now describes the base temporary directory through the shared temporary-directory location and retention guidance rather than only through `--basetemp` configuration wording.

The `tmp_path` fixture documentation now states that it returns a unique `pathlib.Path` temporary directory per test invocation, created as a subdirectory of the base temporary directory with configurable retention described in the shared retention guidance.
The `tmpdir` fixture documentation now mirrors the `tmp_path` description for the legacy path object and points users to the same shared retention guidance.
The release-note-level documented contract clarifies that `--basetemp` still lacks retention across runs under the current behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the `tmp_path` fixture documentation, it should describe a unique per-test temporary directory under a base temporary directory and direct the user to the shared retention guidance.

When a user reads the `tmpdir` fixture documentation, it should describe the same temporary-directory model as `tmp_path`, expressed for the legacy path object, and direct the user to the shared retention guidance.
When a user looks up how the base temp directory is handled, the documentation should present retention behavior through a central explanation rather than scattered, partially duplicated inline text.
When a user relies on `--basetemp`, the documented behavior should make clear that prior run directories are not retained under that option.

task_7.title: Clarify recwarn warnings documentation reference
task_7.description: The 8.3.4 update improves the user-facing documentation for pytest's `recwarn` fixture by directing readers to the canonical warnings reference instead of a hard-coded documentation URL. This is a documentation discoverability fix and does not change runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users reading about the `recwarn` fixture are directed to the canonical warnings documentation for warning categories, without changing how the fixture records warnings.

expectation.grounded: The public documentation for the `recwarn` fixture should refer users to the pytest `warnings` reference for warning-category guidance. The fixture should continue to expose the same `WarningsRecorder`-based behavior and public contract.
expectation.conceptual: Users looking up `recwarn` should be guided to the main warnings documentation through a stable reference, and the fixture itself should behave exactly as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the `recwarn` fixture API, its warning-recording semantics, or the fact that it returns a warning recorder object for captured warnings. The update should be limited to improving the documentation linkage and reference clarity.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade must only improve documentation navigation and clarity. It must not alter observable warning-capture behavior or introduce compatibility changes.

behavior: The `recwarn` fixture documentation now directs readers to the canonical pytest warnings reference for information about warning categories.
The warning-category guidance is expressed as a maintained internal documentation cross-reference rather than a hard-coded external documentation URL.
No runtime behavior changes are introduced for `recwarn`; it continues to provide the same warning-recording functionality.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the `recwarn` fixture documentation, it should point them to the main pytest warnings documentation for warning-category details.
When documentation is rendered across supported documentation versions, the `recwarn` reference should remain stable and not depend on a hard-coded latest-version URL.
When existing code uses `recwarn`, it should observe no change in fixture API or warning-capture behavior after upgrading from 8.3.3 to 8.3.4.

task_8.title: Clarify filterwarnings mark ordering semantics
task_8.description: Pytest 8.3.4 clarifies how multiple warning filters are ordered when using `pytest.mark.filterwarnings`, especially the difference between stacked decorators and `pytestmark`. The release documents existing precedence behavior rather than introducing a runtime change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that documentation for multiple `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` entries clearly explains which warning filter takes precedence when marks are applied as stacked decorators versus when they are provided through `pytestmark`.

expectation.grounded: The upgrade should document the precedence rules for multiple `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` marks. It should state that stacked `@pytest.mark.filterwarnings` decorators follow decorator evaluation order, which is the reverse of the ordering commonly expected from repeated `warnings.filterwarnings` calls, while `pytestmark` entries preserve their listed order. The clarification should present these as existing semantics of `pytest.mark.filterwarnings`, not as a new warning-filtering behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to read the documentation and reliably determine how multiple warning filters are applied in different declaration styles, so they can predict which filter wins without trial and error.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce new runtime behavior, new public APIs, or changed warning-handling semantics. Preserve the existing behavior of `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` and only clarify the ordering and precedence expectations for multiple marks.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should improve clarity only. Existing warning filtering behavior should remain unchanged, and the guidance should avoid implying a behavioral regression or new feature.

behavior: The 8.3.4 update does not add runtime code changes in the provided patch; it documents existing `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` precedence semantics.
When multiple `@pytest.mark.filterwarnings` decorators are stacked, the effective precedence follows decorator evaluation order rather than the intuitive top-to-bottom order of the decorator list.
When multiple warning filters are supplied via `pytestmark`, the effective precedence follows the listed mark order instead of the reversed stacked-decorator ordering.
acceptance_criteria: When a user consults the 8.3.4 documentation for multiple `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` marks, it should explicitly distinguish stacked decorators from `pytestmark` usage.

When the documentation describes stacked `@pytest.mark.filterwarnings` decorators, it should make clear that the applicable precedence order is reversed relative to repeated `warnings.filterwarnings` calls.
When the documentation describes `pytestmark` with multiple `pytest.mark.filterwarnings` marks, it should make clear that precedence follows the order in which the marks are listed.
The documentation should present these rules as clarification of existing behavior, without implying that upgrading to 8.3.4 changes runtime warning filtering.

task_9.title: Clarify Python 3.13 pdb stop-location compatibility
task_9.description: Pytest 8.3.4 acknowledges Python 3.13 debugger behavior where entering pdb through pytest.set_trace() can stop on the trace call itself instead of the following line. This update is an internal compatibility adjustment and should be understood as preserving supported debugging behavior rather than adding a new runtime feature.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that interactive debugging through pytest.set_trace() remains treated as supported on Python 3.13 even when pdb stops at the trace call itself instead of the next executable line, including usage outside a test function and during pytest_generate_tests.

expectation.grounded: When pytest.set_trace() is invoked under Python 3.13, entering Pdb should still be considered successful if the debugger stops on the pytest.set_trace() call rather than a later statement. This expectation applies both to module-level usage outside a test and to invocation from the pytest_generate_tests hook during collection.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading should preserve interactive debugging compatibility on Python 3.13. If a debugger session opens correctly, consumers should treat that as working behavior even if the initial stopped line differs from older Python versions.

constraints.grounded: Do not require a single exact stopped source line as part of the behavioral contract across Python versions. The change should not imply new public APIs, new error conditions, or different collection/execution flow beyond the observed debugger stop location.
constraints.conceptual: The supported outcome is successful entry into the debugger, not a specific line display format. Existing behavior on other Python versions should remain acceptable, and the upgrade should not be interpreted as changing normal test execution semantics.

behavior: On Python 3.13, invoking pytest.set_trace() may enter Pdb with the current frame positioned at the pytest.set_trace() call itself instead of the next executable statement.
This debugger stop-location behavior can be observed both when pytest.set_trace() is used at module scope and when it is used from pytest_generate_tests during collection.
The meaningful observable contract is that an interactive Pdb session is entered successfully; the exact first displayed source line is version-dependent.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest.set_trace() is executed at module scope under Python 3.13, it should still open an interactive Pdb session even if the current line shown is the trace call itself.

When pytest.set_trace() is executed from pytest_generate_tests under Python 3.13, it should still open an interactive Pdb session during collection even if the current line shown is the trace call itself.
Consumers upgrading to 8.3.4 should not need to rely on a specific first stopped line to determine whether pytest.set_trace() behaved correctly.
